explanation: A census is taken every 10 years. Detailed census information is kept confidential for 100 years before release.

angles.q: How often does the UK carry out a census?
alts: The UK census is held at what interval?
How frequently is the population of the UK formally counted?

tf.s: The UK population has become more diverse over time.
tf.e: True. Migration and longer life expectancy have both shaped the population.

tf.s: England has by far the largest share of the UK population.
tf.e: True. England has about 84%, Scotland about 8%, Wales about 5% and Northern Ireland about 3%.

tf.s: People in the UK are living longer than in the past.
tf.e: True. This means more elderly people and increasing pressure on pensions and health services.

explanation: The UK is a tolerant society. Everyone has the right to practise a religion, change it, or have none at all.

angles.q: Which of these describes religious freedom in the UK?
angles.a: Everyone may practise a religion, change it, or have none
wrong: Everyone must belong to the Church of England
Religion is banned in public life
alts: What does freedom of religion mean in the UK?

tf.s: Baptists, Methodists and Presbyterians are Protestant groups in the UK.
tf.e: True. Quakers are another Protestant group.

tf.s: The Church of England is the established Church in Northern Ireland.
tf.e: False. There is no established Church in Northern Ireland or Wales.

tf.s: Bishops of the Church of England are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister.
tf.e: True. The monarch makes the appointment on that advice.

explanation: Festivals celebrated in the UK include Christmas, Easter, Diwali, Eid, Hanukkah, Vaisakhi, Hogmanay, Halloween and Bonfire Night.

angles.q: Hanukkah is celebrated by which religious community?
Vaisakhi is celebrated by which religious community?
alts: Which faith community marks Vaisakhi in April?

tf.s: Diwali is known as the festival of lights.
tf.e: True. It is celebrated by Hindus and Sikhs in the autumn and lasts five days.

tf.s: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year celebration.
tf.e: True. In Scotland 2 January is also a public holiday.

tf.s: In Scotland, 2 January is also a public holiday.
tf.e: True. New Year, or Hogmanay, is a bigger celebration in Scotland than elsewhere in the UK.

tf.s: Mothering Sunday falls three weeks before Easter.
tf.e: True. Father's Day is the third Sunday in June.

tf.s: April Fool's jokes traditionally stop at midday.
tf.e: True. April Fool's Day falls on 1 April.

explanation: Traditional foods differ across the UK: roast beef in England, haggis in Scotland, Welsh cakes in Wales and the Ulster fry in Northern Ireland.

angles.q: Which traditional dish is eaten with roast beef in England?
alts: Roast beef in England is traditionally served with what?

tf.s: Fish and chips is a popular dish across the UK.
tf.e: True. Regional dishes include roast beef in England, haggis in Scotland and Welsh cakes in Wales.

tf.s: Haggis is a traditional dish of Wales.
tf.e: False. Haggis is Scottish. Welsh cakes are the traditional dish of Wales.

explanation: The UK has produced many sporting champions and hosts world-famous events including Wimbledon, the Open and the Grand National.

angles.q: In which sport did Sir Ian Botham represent England?
alts: Sir Ian Botham was a champion in which sport?

angles.q: In which sport did Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean win Olympic gold?
alts: Torvill and Dean are famous in which sport?

angles.q: In which sport did Dame Ellen MacArthur set a world record?
alts: Dame Ellen MacArthur is famous for an achievement in which sport?

tf.s: Sir Chris Hoy is a champion cyclist.
tf.e: True. The Scottish cyclist has won six Olympic gold medals.

tf.s: Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson competed in Paralympic wheelchair racing.
tf.e: True. She won 11 Paralympic gold medals and now sits in the House of Lords.

tf.s: Sir Roger Bannister was the first man to run a mile in under four minutes.
tf.e: True. He did so in 1954, breaking a barrier long thought impossible.

tf.s: The Six Nations is a cricket competition.
tf.e: False. The Six Nations is a rugby union competition. The Ashes is the famous cricket series.

explanation: The UK has a rich cultural life, with music, theatre, art, literature and film all celebrated by national awards and festivals.

angles.q: Which festival of classical music is organised by the BBC each summer?
alts: Which eight-week classical music season does the BBC run?

angles.q: Which Welsh festival celebrates music and poetry?
alts: Wales holds which annual festival of music and poetry?

tf.s: The Notting Hill Carnival celebrates British West Indian culture.
tf.e: True. It is held in London each August.

tf.s: Glastonbury is a well-known UK music festival.
tf.e: True. Others include the Isle of Wight Festival and the V Festival.

tf.s: The Turner Prize is named after the painter JMW Turner.
tf.e: True. The prize, established in 1984, recognises British contemporary artists.

tf.s: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote comic operas.
tf.e: True. Their works include HMS Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance and The Mikado.

explanation: British literature includes the work of Shakespeare, Chaucer, Austen, Dickens, the Brontes, Hardy, Orwell, Conan Doyle and many others.

angles.q: Which author wrote Far from the Madding Crowd?
alts: Far from the Madding Crowd was written by whom?

angles.q: Which author created the character of James Bond?
alts: The James Bond novels were written by whom?

angles.q: Which author is famous for detective novels including Murder on the Orient Express?
alts: Which British writer is the best-known author of detective fiction?

tf.s: Shakespeare wrote both plays and sonnets.
tf.e: True. Many of his plays were first performed at the Globe Theatre in London.

tf.s: The Canterbury Tales was written by Geoffrey Chaucer.
tf.e: True. It is a series of poems in English about pilgrims travelling to Canterbury.

tf.s: William Wordsworth was one of the Romantic poets.
tf.e: True. The Romantics were inspired by nature and human emotion.

explanation: Popular leisure activities in the UK include gardening, sport, cinema, eating out, and visiting historic places.

angles.q: Which flower show held in London is known internationally?
alts: The UK's most famous gardening event is which show?

tf.s: Many people in the UK rent an allotment to grow food.
tf.e: True. An allotment is a small plot of land rented for growing vegetables and flowers.

tf.s: Ealing Studios is famous for British comedy films.
tf.e: True. It produced a celebrated run of comedies in the 1940s and 1950s.

tf.s: A television licence is needed to watch live TV in the UK.
tf.e: True. The licence fee funds the BBC.

tf.s: Dog owners must clean up after their dogs in public places.
tf.e: True. In public places dogs must also wear a collar showing the owner's name and address.

explanation: The UK has many places of interest, including national parks, castles, cathedrals and World Heritage Sites.

angles.q: Which landmark on the Northern Ireland coast is a World Heritage Site?
alts: The rock formation on the north-east coast of Northern Ireland is called what?

angles.q: Which observation wheel stands on the South Bank in London?
alts: The giant wheel beside the Thames is known as what?

tf.s: Edinburgh Castle stands on an extinct volcano.
tf.e: True. It has dominated the city skyline for centuries.

tf.s: The Lake District is England's largest national park.
tf.e: True. It lies in Cumbria and is famous for its lakes and fells.

tf.s: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
tf.e: True. Ben Nevis in Scotland is the highest in the UK.

tf.s: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the UK.
tf.e: True. Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.

tf.s: Yeoman Warders guard Windsor Castle.
tf.e: False. Yeoman Warders, known as Beefeaters, guard the Tower of London.

explanation: Charities play a large part in UK life, and many people give money or volunteer their time to support them.

angles.q: Which charity preserves historic buildings and countryside in the UK?
alts: Which organisation looks after historic houses and coastline for the nation?

tf.s: Many people in the UK volunteer their time for charities.
tf.e: True. Volunteering is one of the main ways of taking part in community life.

tf.s: Charity shops sell goods donated by the public.
tf.e: True. They are a common way of supporting a charity, either by giving or by volunteering.
